sections.h2: Is an Amarillo house taxed by Potter County or Randall County?
sections.html:
Either, depending on where the parcel sits, because Amarillo straddles the county line. Each county has its own tax assessor-collector, but one office values property for both: the Potter-Randall Appraisal District.

The Comptroller's county directories name the units that can show up on an Amarillo bill: the City of Amarillo, Amarillo Independent School District, Amarillo Junior College District, the county, and in some addresses Bushland ISD, River Road ISD, Highland Park ISD, Canyon ISD or High Plains Underground Water Conservation District No. 1.

  • Potter County Tax Assessor-Collector: 900 S. Polk St., Suite 106, Amarillo, 806-342-2600, mail to P.O. Box 2289, Amarillo 79105-2289.
  • Randall County Tax Assessor-Collector: 501 16th St., Suite 200, Canyon, 806-468-5540, mail to P.O. Box 997, Canyon 79015-0997.
  • Potter-Randall Appraisal District: 5701 Hollywood Rd., Amarillo, 806-358-1601, for values, exemptions and protests in both counties.

sections.h2: What tax rate did Amarillo set for 2026/2027?
sections.html:
The city's budget news page gives a total of $0.43070 per $100 of valuation: $0.32412 for maintenance and operations and $0.10658 for existing debt. Council approved the 2026/2027 budget with that rate by a 4-1 vote at a special meeting in late September 2026.

The city says the budget brings in $2,063,963 more property tax revenue than the year before, a 2.58 percent rise, and that $1,295,675 of the increase comes from newly added property. It describes the maintenance and operations rate as effectively 2.9 percent higher, which it equates to about $9 on a $100,000 home.

The same page charts what Amarillo gives back to businesses through development deals: rebates under Chapter 311 and Chapter 380 agreements, and abatements under Chapter 312. For 2024/2025 the city lists $1,143,899 abated by the city itself out of $2,959,496 abated by every participating taxing entity.

sections.h2: What deadlines and penalties apply to an Amarillo tax bill?
sections.html:
Bills mail around October 1 and are payable through January 31. The next day the balance is delinquent, with a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest attached immediately.

The penalty then grows one point a month through June, reaching 12 percent on July 1, while interest keeps running at 1 percent monthly. A unit with an attorney contract can add up to 20 percent for collection. Owners 65 or older, disabled owners and disabled veterans may split a homestead bill into installments, and some collectors allow plans of up to 36 months. To ask for a waiver of penalty and interest, pay promptly and make the request in writing before day 181 after delinquency.

Anyone behind should call the Potter or Randall office right away and, if possible, before January 31.

sections.h2: How does the Potter-Randall Appraisal District help owners with exemptions?
sections.html:
Its website runs an online homestead and over-65 portal, a notice-of-estimated-taxes page with a registration option for alerts, and a login portal where owners can see valuations and file appeals or exemptions. A 2026 Disaster Declaration and Exemption item sits at the top of the news feed, and the home page also publishes a 7.75% basic capitalization rate for 2026 low-income housing valuations.

State law supplies the amounts. The school district share is cut by $140,000 of homestead value, and people 65 or older or disabled get $60,000 more plus a freeze on the school tax. Cities, counties and colleges may add local exemptions of up to 20 percent, so ask which ones Amarillo, Potter County, Randall County and Amarillo Junior College District have adopted. A disabled veteran's exemption runs from $5,000 at a 10 to 29 percent rating to $12,000 at 70 percent or more, and a 100 percent rating can cover the whole residence homestead.

  • General filing deadline: before May 1, though some veteran claims can be filed up to five years after the delinquency date.
  • Heirs without a recorded deed in their name can claim homestead with an affidavit of ownership interest, a death certificate and a recent utility bill.

sections.h2: How can an Amarillo owner protest an appraised value?
sections.html:
File a written protest with the appraisal district by May 15, or within 30 days of receiving the value notice if that is later. Homestead notices begin arriving around April 1, and the appraisal review board starts hearings about mid-May.

Only market value can be contested, since the district does not set rates. After the first qualifying year, a homestead's assessed value can rise at most 10 percent a year even when the market jumps faster. A loss at the board leaves district court, binding arbitration, or for values over $1,000,000 the State Office of Administrative Hearings. One district serves both counties, so there is no separate county filing, but the undisputed amount should reach the Potter or Randall collector before delinquency while the protest is pending.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about Amarillo households?
sections.html:
The July 2025 estimate is 205,130 residents, against 200,393 in 2020 and 190,695 in 2010, across 102.30 land square miles. About 59.7 percent of homes are owner occupied with a median value of $196,900 for 2020 to 2024. Renters pay a median $1,092, owners with a mortgage $1,654, and the median household earns $65,912.

The city has 79,741 households averaging 2.50 people and 10,973 veterans. Adults with a bachelor's degree are 26.6 percent, and 89.2 percent of households have broadband. Retail sales reached $5,722,271 thousand in 2022, and health care and social assistance receipts $2,777,390 thousand.

sections.h2: How does a tax lien affect an Amarillo sale?
sections.html: A Texas tax lien attaches on January 1, follows the property and keeps the person who owned it that day personally liable even after a sale. Title cannot clear until the back taxes are settled. An owner with accounts in both counties, for instance on adjoining parcels, should ask each tax office for a separate payoff letter before closing.

sections.h2: What happens when an Amarillo house goes to a tax sale?
sections.html:
The taxing units can foreclose on the lien and auction the property, usually through the constable or an agent the unit hires. Texas keeps no statewide sale calendar, so watch the Potter and Randall county sites and clerk postings.

A former owner can still reclaim a homestead, farm or mineral interest for two years from the date the purchaser's deed is filed, paying the purchase price plus a 25 percent premium in year one or 50 percent in year two, along with recording fees, taxes, penalties, interest and costs. Other property has a 180-day window and a premium of no more than 25 percent. Money left after the sale belongs to the former owner for two years. A purchaser owes an itemized cost list within 10 days of a written request.

faqs.q: Is Amarillo in Potter County or Randall County?
faqs.a: Both. The city lies across the two counties, so the bill comes from the county where the parcel sits. The Potter-Randall Appraisal District values property in both.

faqs.q: What is the Amarillo city tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: The total on the city's budget news page is $0.43070 per $100 of valuation: $0.32412 for maintenance and operations and $0.10658 for debt.

faqs.q: When do Amarillo property taxes go delinquent?
faqs.a: February 1, after a January 31 due date. A 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest attach at once, and the penalty reaches 12 percent on July 1.

faqs.q: Who do I call to pay Amarillo property taxes?
faqs.a: Call the county office for your parcel: Potter County at 806-342-2600 or Randall County at 806-468-5540. Use the Potter-Randall Appraisal District at 806-358-1601 for value and exemption questions.

faqs.q: How large is the homestead exemption in Amarillo?
faqs.a: State law removes $140,000 of homestead value from the school tax base, plus $60,000 for owners 65 or older or disabled. Cities and counties may add local exemptions of up to 20 percent.
